title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task with gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120). A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applied intent-constraint and workflow-policy checks and could trigger ≤1 repair when validator.violation_count>0. Outcomes: baseline success = 120/120 (1.00); guarded success = 120/120 (1.00); contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Validator traces show repair_applied=false for all guarded episodes. We expand preregistered design details, execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, statistical interpretation of the degenerate ceiling outcome, reproducibility guidance grounded in archived artifacts, and limitations affecting generalization.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into network configuration commands, promising faster NetOps workflows. Yet plausible-looking candidate commands can violate workflow policies (for example, requiring shutdown before MTU change or safe make-before-break uplink switchover), cause regressions, or break operational invariants. To mitigate such semantic failures many proposals recommend integrating verification, emulation, or veto layers into LLM-driven pipelines so generated candidates are checked and, when necessary, repaired before enactment. Closed-loop, executable tests (digital twins or emulators) are required to reveal failures beyond token- or syntax-level correctness.

This study asks a precise mechanistic question, preregistered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1: Does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To isolate the validator/repair marginal effect from generation variance we used a shared-initial-candidate paired design: for each task the exact same generated candidate was evaluated under both conditions. This design answers whether a validator/repair stage can improve outcomes for identical generator outputs. We emphasize that the design intentionally removes generation variance and therefore addresses a narrower question than open-ended multi-model evaluations.
sections.related_work:
Recent benchmarks and architectural reports emphasize that evaluation limited to generated-text correctness misses operational failure modes. Executable benchmark efforts such as NetConfArena and related emulation-grounded suites examine closed-loop agentic behavior and reveal semantic failure classes absent from text-only checks. Tool papers and surveys propose generate→validate→repair architectures, digital twins, and guardrail patterns (veto layers, canaries, model→formal-model translation) to improve trustworthiness in agentic NetOps. Our contribution is methodological: a preregistered, artifact-rich paired test that holds the generator fixed to isolate the validator/repair mechanism.

The literature identifies several evidence gaps that motivated our preregistered exploratory agenda: scarcity of large production-rooted misconfiguration corpora with verifiable ground truth; limited cross-model comparisons under identical executable harnesses; and under-explored methods to provide calibrated, actionable uncertainty on structured configuration outputs. These gaps informed our emphasis on deterministic archival artifacts and explicit instrumentation so future runs can reuse the same task bank, validator, and manifests for comparable studies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design: The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) and archived before execution. The preregistration specified a paired-binary confirmatory design with exactly N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks, deterministically assigned into three topology classes (40 tasks per class: edge, core, leaf–spine). Each task produced a single shared initial candidate generated by gpt-5-mini; the pairing parameter independent_condition_generation=false enforces identical generator outputs across conditions. The preregistration constrained repairs to at most one repair iteration per guarded episode and declared the primary estimand as the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with the exact two-sided McNemar as the prespecified test.

Generation and prompt/pipeline semantics: All shared initial candidates were produced by the declared hosted model (gpt-5-mini) and recorded in execution/responses/*. Each shared-initial generation stage was invoked exactly once per pair (execution manifest: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 120). The archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) records the declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", max_output_tokens = 1500, requested_model = "gpt-5-mini", and store=false. The run used a single shared initial generation per pair so that any downstream difference depends only on validator/repair processing of identical text output.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair logic: The guarded pipeline integrated the deterministic emulator validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that executes task-encoded workflow policies (for example: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break patterns). For every episode the validator produces a structured validator_trace containing validation_before and validation_after states, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and a boolean repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy applied a single repair iteration only when validator.violation_count>0 and archived any repair_provider_trace. Repair artifacts were to be stored under execution/scoring/ when used; none exist because no repairs were applied.

Task generation and difficulty metadata: The task bank is a deterministic synthetic corpus produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task_manifest entry contains the initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence (the correct command ordering), and machine-readable constraints. Tasks are labeled with difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, and a qualitative level: medium/hard/very_hard) to permit stratified analyses. Representative task manifests and response files (for example, execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt) are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

Instrumentation, contamination controls, and exclusion rules: The harness logged provider-call audits, enforced deterministic emulator-state resets between tasks (container image checks and seeds), and ran contamination heuristics (duplicate-output detection and cross-condition cache-key reuse). Exclusion rules in the preregistration excluded task pairs only when harness instrumentation or emulator provisioning failed; such exclusions would be logged and archived. analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv record contamination and missingness summaries for the run.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting: The run completed planned episodes (execution/manifest: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240) and produced one shared initial generation per pair (model_calls_used = 120). No model-provider failures, caching anomalies, contamination flags, or instrumentational exclusions were recorded (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty; analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 and zero failed episodes). The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms completed_episode_count = 240, complete_pair_count = 120, and provider_call_audit showing hosted_model_call_event_count = 120.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency: analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline = 120 successes, 0 failures (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded = 120 successes, 0 failures (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. The exact two-sided McNemar test therefore yields p = 1.0 and a paired-difference estimate = 0.00.

Bootstrap CI and statistical degeneracy: We computed a bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the paired difference with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729 (recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Because the empirical paired table contains no discordant pairs, every bootstrap resample reproduces n_11=120 and yields paired-difference = 0.00; consequently the bootstrap percentile CI is degenerate [0.00, 0.00]. This degenerate CI is an artifact of resampling an empirical distribution with zero observed discordance and reflects no observable variability in the recorded paired outcomes under the shared-generation design.

Per-topology aggregates and representative traces: Tasks were deterministically assigned 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology archived success counts are: Edge 40/40 baseline and 40/40 guarded; Core 40/40 baseline and 40/40 guarded; Leaf–spine 40/40 baseline and 40/40 guarded. Representative scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and task-000001-guarded.json) show normalized_response matching normalized_reference_answer, parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count, validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true, and validator_trace.repair_applied = false. These artifacts illustrate how the validator parsed commands, enumerated required steps, and recorded zero violations for these examples.

Repair activity and secondary endpoints: The preregistered guarded repair policy required repair_applied only when validator.violation_count>0. For this run violation_count = 0 for every guarded episode; repair_applied = false across the archive and no repair_provider_trace artifacts exist. Consequently preregistered secondary estimands (proportion of tasks requiring repair, mean repair calls per successful task) are vacuous in this dataset.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the ceiling outcome: The shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair effects by removing generation variance. Under this design the guarded pipeline can only change outcomes if it (a) detects violations that were present in the shared candidate and (b) successfully repairs them. In our archived run the shared initial candidates produced by gpt-5-mini satisfied the deterministic emulator validator's intent constraints and workflow policies for every task; hence all pairs were concordant successes (n_11=120). The guarded pipeline therefore had no opportunity to apply repairs, producing a ceiling/null outcome (paired difference = 0.00).

Methodological implications: The null result answers the narrow mechanistic question posed by the design — for identical generator outputs produced under the declared prompting and model, the validator/repair stage did not change outcomes because no violations were present. This does not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary in operational practice. In more realistic settings generator variance, prompt perturbations, adversarial inputs, or alternative model families may produce invalid candidates for which a validator/repair subsystem could be decisive. To measure practical repair utility future confirmatory designs should allow independent per-condition generation or explicitly inject generator errors so repair behavior can be exercised.

Design recommendations supported by artifacts: The archived task_manifest.jsonl includes difficulty metadata (dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, and qualitative level) that permits stratified selection of tasks expected to produce higher generator error rates. Future runs should (1) allow independent generation per condition, (2) increase repair budget above one iteration per episode, (3) test multiple generator models and prompt perturbations, and (4) incorporate multi-vendor or telemetry-limited validators. The execution and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, deterministic_reconciliation.json) provide deterministic bookkeeping templates for such expanded designs.

Threats to validity and limitations (artifact-grounded): Internal validity — prompt sensitivity is constrained by the shared-generation design; retries and provider-call auditing are archived (provider_call_audit shows cache_miss_count = 120 and no failed_hosted_model_call_event_count). Construct validity — the deterministic emulator validator operationalizes semantic correctness using task-encoded workflow policies; this deterministic operationalization may omit production failure modes. External validity — the task bank is synthetic and deterministic (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), so generalization to multi-vendor, partially observable production networks is limited. Conclusion validity — the preregistered power planning assumed a baseline failure rate ≈0.40 and targeted a 15 percentage-point absolute reduction; because baseline success was 100% the preregistered power assumptions were not met and the primary test is uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.

Operational implications and auditability: Despite the ceiling outcome, archived validator traces demonstrate reproducible, structured decision records (validation_before/after, touched-field counts, violation lists) that can be surfaced to operators for audit and post-hoc analysis. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts provide a template for accountable runs: recording model_calls_used, stage accounting, provider-call audits, and artifact manifests supports operator-facing auditability and independent replay.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness and a single declared model (gpt-5-mini). Every shared initial candidate satisfied the deterministic emulator validator, producing n_11=120 concordant successes and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The degenerate outcome documents a ceiling effect on this curated synthetic task bank and illustrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear under independent generation. Our principal contribution is methodological and reproducibility-oriented: we show how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and provide deterministic archived artifacts (model configuration, task manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis outputs) to enable follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, vary generator families, or expand repair budgets.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
